From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. # Wattlebridge Holdings - Seller Document Review

## Internal Assessment: Departures from Buyer Playbook

### 1. General Warranty Cap: CRITICAL DEPARTURE

**Seller position:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap.

**Our position:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 is the starting position; the 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is conditional and has **zero prior written authority from Amelia Frost**. The cap falls *below* our baseline by AUD 1,200,000.

**Reasoning:** The cap is fundamental to our acquisition risk model. Below our accepted range means we're leaving ~50% of the margin between our cap and a typical market standard on the table before anything else happens. This should be raised to at least 30% (AUD 7,200,000) or 35% (AUD 8,400,000), or we should obtain Amelia's explicit sign-off first. Either way, no agreement until resolved.

---

### 2. De minimis & Basket: Critical Departure + Hidden Regime Override

**Seller position:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000.

**Our position:** De minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.

**Reasoning:** These thresholds are ~5× below ours. They also create a perception that claims below AUD 25,000 are "de minimis" — meaning the buyer effectively cedes claims in that narrow band without compensation. Our threshold is minimal (only a token $5K de minimis). The basket of $250K also seems deliberately low, suggesting the seller may have historical claims in the low hundreds of thousands that fall outside our buyer's economic interest.

**Hidden issue flagged:** Under "Tax/IP: settled under general regime" — the seller explicitly proposes tax and IP warranties under the same general-cap framework. Our playbook keeps Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories **separate**. A hidden general-regime override would apply to tax and IP claims that deserve their own treatment, potentially collapsing those entirely into the same 20% / $4.8M bucket where they should rest on their own footing.

---

### 3. Time Limits: Departure + Structural Problem

**Seller position:** General claims within 18 months post-Completion. Seller proposes any limitation applies to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

**Our position:** 24 months post-Completion; the 18-month fallback requires Amelia Frost written approval (none given). The "any limitation applies to all" position is dangerous — it effectively extends limitation periods by treating non-warranty-specific periods as opexions.

**Reasoning:** 18 months is well below our 24-month baseline. More critically, the seller's "all Claims" broad reading could be used to extend claim time limits for fundamental/title claims, which under our playbook have their own separate, longer regime. We need specific carving out of the fundamental/title period — 24 months minimum, ideally 4–5 years — and we must refuse the blanket extension.

---

### 4. Limitations & Reliance: Overly Broad

**Seller position:** Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to *all* claims of any nature, without qualification.

**Our position:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve out of *all* caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.

**Reasoning:** The seller's absolute position risks being read as a waiver of fraud protections. The power of fraud carve-outs in Australian law is significant — we cannot permit the seller to contract away fraud protections entirely. We must insist on an express carve-out, and the cap application must still allow fraud claims to punch through.

---

### 5. Bluefen Consent: Insufficient Basis

**Seller position:** Uses reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery.

**Our position:** Effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied *before* Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.

**Reasoning:** DD-002 shows the seller has NOT included final written consent or evidence of satisfied conditions. A change-control of ~$3.6M revenue (30% of FY26) is material. If conditions aren't met pre-Completion and the consent isn't obtained in writing, the buyer faces a regulatory/compliance exposure for failing to get a required change-control outcome. This is a specific disclosure gap — see disclosure §2 — but the gap is structural, not disclosed away.

---

### 6. Riverlark Facility: Post-Completion Release Only

**Seller position:** Release provided following Completion only.

**Our position:** Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

**Reasoning:** The facility has ~AUD 3.2M outstanding and isn't repaid as of 22 Sept 2026. A post-Completion release leaves the buyer with $3.2M of debt to clean up immediately after closing. For a cash-free, debt-free deal, this materially threatens the balance sheet position. We require full repayment from Completion funds and an irrevocable undertaking.

---

### 7. Employee Bonuses (DD-005): Silent Exclusion

**Seller position:** Not separately itemised in funds flow; disclosure doesn't state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

**Our position:** DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.

**Reasoning:** AUD 420K in contingent bonuses is a material contingency for any purchaser, especially with payroll tax, superannuation, and on-costs potentially triggered. The deal structure (debt-free/cash-free) depends on clean separation. Silent exclusion in the funds flow is a governance failure. We need the line item, plus disbursement schedule and tax incidence either disclosed or funded at buyer cost.

---

### 8. Ironquay IP: Weakening the Indemnity

**Seller position:** Existing indemnity limited to SOW3 payment (AUD 180K); considered adequate.

**Our position:** Broaden the indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180K is not independently verified either way.

**Reasoning:** The SOW3 cure is a genuine protection mechanism — we preserve it by accepting the AUD 180K cap tied to the existing disbursement condition. But beyond that, the AUD 180K figure lacks independent bank verification (disclosure §4 confirms this). That means the number could understate actual amounts owed. We want broader coverage beyond the existing cure mechanism.

---

### 9. Export/Privacy Incident (DD-006): Materials-on-Delivery Position

**Seller position:** Preliminary operational matter; no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand established.

**Our position:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach but treat disclosure obligation seriously given prior incidents are known.

**Reasoning:** The disclosure itself admits uncertainty about scope (~1,240 records), access, and notification duty. This is exactly the kind of exposure our playbook flags — the disclosure letter doesn't characterise the matter as confirmed breach (good), but the uncertainty is real. We need log preservation signed off, periodic investigation updates, and the investigation scope expanded beyond "preliminary." If evidence emerges later, we will move fast with remedies.

---

### 10. Sandbar Renewals (AUD 330K): Concealment Risk

**Seller position:** Ordinary-course operating costs.

**Our position:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

**Reasoning:** Three renewals totaling AUD 330K that aren't separately characterised — "ordinary course" is a conclusion, not a disclosure. If these renewals involve term changes, termination triggers, or falling outside ordinary course (e.g., strategic supply changes), the deal structure would be materially affected. The seller shouldn't classify without disclosure. We need annual renewal terms, terminability status, and whether each was accrued at time of transaction.

---

### 11. Title Evidence: Self-Reported Source

**Seller position:** DD-012 share register shows Harbourglass Ventures holds 100%.

**Our position:** Require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

**Reasoning:** A corporate share register is not independent proof — it's self-reported evidence from the seller's own bookkeeping. Potential encumbrances, assignments, or third-party transfers can exist in the registers without the seller disclosing them. We need independent third-party evidence: registers of members, transfer forms, encumbrance disclosures, and ideally the title opinion itself.

---

### 12. Tax/IP Settled in General Regime: Hidden Override

As noted above, the seller explicitly wants tax and IP warranties under the general regime, removing the category separation our playbook insists on. This is a fundamental structural departure — tax and IP exposures deserve their own caps and time limits; assigning them to the general bucket collapses protection where it matters most and could leave unrecovered material contingent liabilities.

---

# Recommendation Summary

| # | Issue | Response | Urgency |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cap dropped to 20% / $4.8M | Restore to ≥30% (~$7.2M) or secure Amelia's written authority | High |
| 2 | Thresholds $25K/$250K vs $5K/$50K | Push back on both; maintain our baseline | High |
| 3 | 18-month vs 24-month period | Restore 24 months; carve out fundamental/title 24–48 mo | High |
| 4 | Broad limitations apply to all claims | Carve out fraud/wilful concealment; seller cannot waive protections | High |
| 5 | Bluefen consent not effective pre-Completion | Require effective consent + evidence of satisfied conditions **before** Close | Medium-High |
| 6 | Riverlark post-Completion release only | Require repayment from Completion funds + irrevocable undertaking | High |
| 7 | DD-005 bonuses silent in funds flow | Require specific line item + disbursement schedule + funding resolution | High |
| 8 | Ironquay AUD 180K not independently verified | Broaden beyond SOW3 cure; keep cure intact | Medium |
| 9 | DD-006 undisclosed uncertainty | Request log preservation, ongoing investigation updates, expanded scope | Medium |
| 10 | Sandbar renewals classified as ordinary course | Request detailed renewal terms for each; assess terminability/accrual | Medium |
| 11 | DD-012 share register = self-reported source | Require independent third-party title evidence including encumbrances | Medium |
| 12 | Tax/IP collapsed into general regime | Restore separate Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories | High |

### Recommended Course of Action

1. **Begin mark-up immediately.** The cap, thresholds, time limits, fraud carve-out, Bluefen, Riverlark, and funds flow are the five most urgent items.
2. **Run the tax/IP separation through every clause** — no general clause referencing "all claims" or the "general liability cap" should cover tax or IP warranties without explicit exception language.
3. **Confirm Amelia Frost's written authority** for any conditional fallback (notably the 20% cap and 18-month period) before engaging further — or assert our starting position directly and hold firm.
4. **Escalate DD-005 and the DD-006 uncertainty** to the due diligence team for financial modelling and external legal review respectively, since both directly affect purchase price and risk allocation.
